nodes.name: Ultrafast microwave quasi-solid-state construction
nodes.procedure: Ultrafast (20 s) microwave quasi-solid approach was used to synthesize the osmium-osmium phosphide (Os-OsP₂) catalyst with heterogeneous junction. The synthesized product via the quasi-solid microwave-assisted combustion approach primarily consists of two phases: OsP₂ (PDF#34-0334) and Os (PDF#06-0662).

nodes.characterization_summary: The synthesized Os-OsP₂ catalyst primarily consists of two phases: OsP₂ (PDF#34-0334) and Os (PDF#06-0662).
nodes.evidence_snippet: To validate the crystal structure of the synthesized catalyst, X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis was conducted (Figure 1b). The synthesized product via the quasi-solid microwave-assisted combustion approach primarily consists of two phases: OsP₂ (PDF#34-0334) and Os (PDF#06-0662) (Figures S1 and S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images reveal a dense and compact bulk structure for Os-OsP₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal a dense and compact bulk structure (Figure S3, Supporting Information), which ensures structural stability and uniform charge distribution across the material.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows mixture of nanoflakes and granular structure for Os-OsP₂; heterojunction interface visible with 0.24 nm spacing for Os (100) plane and 0.20 nm for OsP₂ (220) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was employed to further examine the microscopic morphology of the Os-OsP₂ sample. ... Upon magnification (Figure 1c), the heterojunction interface between Os and OsP₂ becomes clearly visible, with the 0.24 nm spacing corresponding to the (100) crystallographic plane of Os and the 0.20 nm spacing belonging to the (220) crystallographic plane of OsP₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image of Os-OsP₂ shows the heterojunction interface (Figure 1c).
EDS elemental distribution map confirms homogeneous distribution of Os and P throughout the Os-OsP₂ sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental distribution map (Figure 1e) confirms the homogeneous distribution of Os and P throughout the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis shows significant strain differences at the Os-OsP₂ heterojunction interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The geometric phase analysis (GPA) algorithm extracts strain distribution from the TEM images. As shown in Figure 1f, significant strain differences are observed at the heterojunction interface...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of Os-OsP₂ shows Os 4f peaks: Os⁴⁺ at Os 4f₅/₂ (53.69 eV) and Os 4f₇/₂ (51.08 eV), Os⁰ at Os 4f₅/₂ (55.69 eV) and Os 4f₇/₂ (52.93 eV) shifted ≈0.2 eV higher than pure Os and OsP₂; P 2p peaks at P 2p₁/₂ (130.57 eV), P 2p₃/₂ (129.66 eV), and P-O (134 eV) shifted ≈0.3 eV from pure OsP₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis demonstrates that the composition of Os, OsP₂, and the Os-OsP₂ includes Os and P. For Os 4f in Os-OsP₂, the peaks Os 4f₅/₂ (53.69 eV) and Os 4f₇/₂ (51.08 eV) were attributed to Os⁴⁺, Os 4f₅/₂ (55.69 eV) and Os 4f₇/₂ (52.93 eV) attributed to Os⁰ ... corresponding to P2p₁/₂ (130.57 eV), P2p₃/₂ (129.66 eV), and P-O (134 eV) shift ≈0.3 eV in Os-OsP₂ compared with pure OsP₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Os L₃-edge XANES of Os-OsP₂ shows white line peak intensity and absorption edge position close to Os foil, indicating average Os valence close to 0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition to further determine the valence and local coordination environment of Os atoms, the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis of the Os L₃ edges were carried out for both pure Os and heterostructure Os-OsP₂. As shown in Figure 2c, the white line peak intensity and absorption edge position of Os-OsP₂ in XANES at the Os L₃ edge is infinitely close to the Os foil.

nodes.characterization_summary: Os L₃-edge EXAFS fitting shows each Os atom in Os-OsP₂ coordinated to ≈6.0 Os atoms (R=2.363 Å) and 2.0 P atoms (R=2.688 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding EXAFS fitting results show that each Os atom is coordinated to ≈6.0 Os atoms and 2.0 P atoms, and the Os-Os and Os-P distances are 2.363 and 2.688 Å, respectively (Figure 2e and Figure S8 and Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform EXAFS visualizes coexistence of Os-Os and Os-P paths in Os-OsP₂ heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Finally, wavelet transform (WT)-EXAFS (Figure 2f,g) further visualized the coexistence of Os-Os and Os-P paths in the Os-OsP₂ heterostructure.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The catalyst-hydrogen interaction in the reaction was assessed by the Hydrogen temperature-programmed desorption (H₂-TPD) profile study of Os-OsP₂ (Figure S10, Supporting Information). The results show that the hydrogen desorption temperature of Os-OsP₂ is significantly lower than that of Os and OsP₂...
